misconceptions.description: Marks 'First', 'Next' and 'Then' but misses a linking phrase of two or more words such as 'After that' or 'Over the following weeks'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Look at the start of every sentence: a group of words before the comma can link, too.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Makes up an idea the story does not support
misconceptions.description: Gives a guess with no clue behind it, e.g. says Kavya "is late for school" when nothing in the story says so.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask the child to point to the words that made them think it; if there are none, think again.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives no clue, or a clue that does not prove the point
misconceptions.description: Writes a sensible idea with no words from the text, or quotes a line that does not show it, e.g. "It is cold because a stream rushed over stones."
misconceptions.repair_hint: Model the pattern: idea, then 'because the story says ...', then the exact words in quotation marks.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Predicts without using what happened earlier
misconceptions.description: Gives a next event that ignores the clue the story planted, e.g. says "Om's string will snap" when the story told us Riya's string was rough.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Before predicting, find one earlier sentence that points to what will happen.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Picks an exciting ending the story gives no reason for
misconceptions.description: Chooses a surprising event with no link to the story, e.g. "Kabir will find treasure in the sand."
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: which words in the story make this likely? If none, choose a more likely ending.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Talks about only one of the two texts
misconceptions.description: Gives an idea or feature that fits one text but not the other, e.g. "Parathas are tasty."
misconceptions.repair_hint: Check the idea against both texts: does it fit Text A and Text B?

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Picks a detail that does not show the time or place
misconceptions.description: Copies or names something that is the same today, e.g. copies "electricity" when the story says there was none, or "the whole family sat together".
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: would this be different today, or somewhere else? Only those details show when and where.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Names a detail but not how life is different
misconceptions.description: Writes "they had a lantern" and stops, without saying that today we switch on a light.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Use the pattern: 'Then ... but now ...'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up where a story is set with when it is set
misconceptions.description: Gives a place detail when asked about time, e.g. copies "near Satara" when asked what shows it was long ago.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Sort clues into two piles first: clues about where and clues about when.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Takes I inside speech marks as the narrator
misconceptions.description: Says a story is told by a character because a character says "I will bring the colours" inside speech marks.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Cover the words inside speech marks first; then look for I or he and she in what is left.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Thinks the main character is telling the story because the story is about them
misconceptions.description: Says "Rahul is telling the story" when the narrator calls him Rahul and he.
misconceptions.repair_hint: If the story calls the character by name and he or she, someone outside the story is telling it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Misses a narrator who says I because the narrator talks about others
misconceptions.description: Says a story told by an auto-rickshaw is told by an outside narrator because it says "he" about the driver many times.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Look for even one I, my or we outside speech marks: that is the narrator speaking.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Copies a word that does not show who is telling
misconceptions.description: Copies a name or an action word, e.g. "Pallavi" or "ran", when asked for the word that shows the narrator.
misconceptions.repair_hint: The words that show it are I, me, my, we, our, or he, she, they.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives a feeling but no link to their own life
misconceptions.description: Writes "I felt sad for Sahil" and stops, with no time when something like it happened to them.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: when have you felt like that, or been somewhere like that? Add 'This reminds me of ...'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Retells the story instead of responding to it
misconceptions.description: Writes what happened, e.g. "Siya lost her mother and went to the police booth", with no feeling or opinion of their own.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Start with 'I felt ...' or 'I think ...' and say what you think, not what happened.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives a like or dislike with no reason
misconceptions.description: Writes "I liked it" or "I would not do that" with no because.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Every response needs a 'because' linked to the story or their life.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Misses the words that mark an opinion
misconceptions.description: Underlines the topic word, e.g. "lassi", instead of the opinion words "In our opinion" or "best".
misconceptions.repair_hint: Hunt for words like I think, best, delicious, should and in my view.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up nouns and verbs
misconceptions.description: Underlines a naming word when asked for the verb, or an action when asked for the noun: marks dog as the verb in 'The dog barks', or work as a noun in 'helps the farmers work'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: can you do it? Then it is a verb here. Can you see or name it? Then it is a noun. Check the job in this sentence.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Marks names as pronouns, or misses pronouns
misconceptions.description: Underlines a name such as Dev or Grandmother when asked for pronouns, or leaves out it and them.
misconceptions.repair_hint: A pronoun stands in place of a name: he, she, it, we, they, him, her, them. Try swapping the word for a name.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Marks the noun instead of the describing word
misconceptions.description: Underlines boy or bag when asked for the adjectives in 'The tall boy lifted a heavy bag', or puts bright with the nouns.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Find the noun first, then ask: what kind? The word that answers is the adjective.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up words for place and time
misconceptions.description: Writes 'in Sunday' or 'on nine o'clock', or picks inside when asked for the word that tells when.
misconceptions.repair_hint: On for days and dates, at for clock times, in for months; during, until and since tell when.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Picks a place word with the wrong meaning
misconceptions.description: Writes 'on the bed' when the shoes cannot be seen, or 'among two trees' for between.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Picture where the thing is. Act it out with a pencil and a box: under, behind, through, across.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Underlines the thing, not the word that tells where
misconceptions.description: Asked for the word that tells where in 'Kabir hid behind the door', underlines door instead of behind.
misconceptions.repair_hint: The where word comes before the place: ask 'where did he hide?' and point to the small word before the door.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Ignores the time word
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Yesterday Sana visits her grandmother' or 'Every morning Rohan brushed his teeth'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Circle the time word first: yesterday and last week ask for the past; every day asks for the present.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Sorts by the ending, not the time
misconceptions.description: Puts need or feed with the past verbs because they end in -ed, or puts went and ran with the present because they have no -ed.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Put the verb in a sentence with yesterday and one with every day. Which one sounds right?

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Adds -ed to an irregular verb
misconceptions.description: Writes goed, eated, runned or catched for went, ate, ran and caught.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Keep a list of the verbs that change instead of adding -ed. Say them aloud in pairs: go, went; run, ran.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Uses the have-form for the simple past
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Pooja written a letter' or 'the team drunk lassi' for wrote and drank.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Written, drunk and seen need has or have before them. With no helper word, use wrote, drank and saw.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up pasts that sound alike
misconceptions.description: Pairs teach with thought or bring with brought wrongly, or spells caught as cought.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Teach and catch take -aught; think, bring, fight and buy take -ought. Say each pair aloud.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Joining word does not fit the meaning
misconceptions.description: Joins two ideas with a word that changes the sense: 'I wanted to play outside, so it was raining.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the sentence aloud with each joining word. Ask: does it say what really happened?

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Swaps so and because
misconceptions.description: Puts the cause and the result the wrong way round: 'The shop was closed so it was a holiday', or 'It was raining because I wore my raincoat.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Because comes before the reason; so comes before what happened next. Find the reason first.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Joins everything with and
misconceptions.description: Strings ideas together with and each time: 'Priya finished her homework and she went to play and her brother stayed at home.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask how the ideas are linked: in time (after, before, when), by a reason (because, so), or as a contrast (but).

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves a full stop between the joined ideas
misconceptions.description: Writes two sentences with the joining word after the full stop: 'I wore my raincoat. Because it was raining.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: One sentence has one full stop, at the very end. Take out the full stop in the middle.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes the story instead of a plan
misconceptions.description: Writes long full sentences or the whole story in the plan boxes, e.g. 'One day Kabir was going to school on the bus and he forgot...' instead of 'Kabir leaves tiffin on bus'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Show a plan beside a story; cross out every word in a sentence that is not a key word until only notes are left.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Puts a point in the wrong part of the plan
misconceptions.description: Writes the ending note in the beginning box, or a note about food under 'Where it lives', e.g. 'Riya finds her kite at last' in the Beginning box.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask 'What happens first?' and 'How does it finish?' and point to the box for each before writing.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves out a main part
misconceptions.description: Fills the beginning and the middle but leaves the end empty, or plans a story with no problem to solve.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Check the plan with three fingers: beginning, middle, end. Each finger needs a note.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Lists things without describing them
misconceptions.description: Names what is there with no describing words, e.g. 'There is a desk. There is a fan. There is a board.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: For each thing named, ask 'What is it like?' and add one describing word or detail.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Describes only what is seen
misconceptions.description: Every sentence is about looks, with nothing heard, smelt or felt, e.g. 'The market is big. It is red and yellow.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Draw an eye, an ear and a hand; write one sentence for each before writing the description.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Uses general words such as nice and good
misconceptions.description: Writes 'The park was nice and the trees were good' instead of words that show what it was like.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ban nice and good for one piece; make a word bank of exact describing words together first.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Tells what happened instead of describing
misconceptions.description: Writes a story of events ('We went to the station and then the train came') when asked to describe the place.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Freeze the moment like a photo: describe only what is there in that one moment, with no 'then'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes a fact in the wrong box
misconceptions.description: Puts a true fact from the text under the wrong label, e.g. writes 'seeds and insects' in the box for 'Where it lives'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the label aloud as a question ('Where does it live?') and find the sentence that answers it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes what they know, not what the text says
misconceptions.description: Fills a box from their own ideas instead of the passage, e.g. writes 'bananas' for what peacocks eat when the text says seeds.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Before writing, put a finger on the words in the text that give the fact.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Copies a whole sentence into a box
misconceptions.description: Copies the full sentence 'A male peacock has a long tail of green and blue feathers' where the box needs 'green and blue'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Underline only the words that answer the label, and write just those.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes events out of order
misconceptions.description: Tells the end before the middle, e.g. 'We ate the cake. Then Mum baked it.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Number the events on fingers or sticky notes and say them aloud in order before writing.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Links every event with 'and then'
misconceptions.description: Writes one long chain: 'I woke up and then I brushed and then I ate and then I went.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Give a strip of time words (First, Next, After that, Finally) and use a different one for each sentence.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves out a step so the events jump
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Dev bought a kite. He got it down from the tree.' with no sentence saying it got stuck.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the sentences to a partner and ask 'Did you know how we got here?' after each one.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Keeps speech marks and said
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Sana: "Can I have some lassi?" she asked.' keeping the speech marks and the reporting words.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Cover the speech marks and 'said' with a finger: what is left after the name and colon is the line.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves out stage directions
misconceptions.description: Writes only names and words, so the actor does not know to smile, run or look out of the window.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask 'What does the actor do while saying this?' and write the answer in brackets.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes stage directions in the past tense
misconceptions.description: Writes '(Rohan ran to the window)' instead of '(Rohan runs to the window)'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the direction as if telling the actor now: 'runs', 'looks', 'smiles'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Retells the story instead of setting it out
misconceptions.description: Copies the story as sentences with a narrator, e.g. 'Mum came in and she was smiling and said yes.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Put one speaker's name on each new line and only write what that person says.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Suggests a change without saying where or what
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Add more detail' or 'Make it better' without naming the sentence or what is weak in it.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask the child to point to the exact words, then say what a reader is missing there.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Rewrites with the same weakness
misconceptions.description: Rewrites 'The cake was nice' as 'The cake was very nice', still with a word that tells the reader nothing.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Before rewriting, say aloud what is wrong; check the new version does not have it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Only fixes spelling when sense or content is weak
misconceptions.description: Corrects a small spelling slip but leaves the sentence that does not belong, or the missing step, untouched.
misconceptions.repair_hint: First read for sense: does every sentence fit, and is anything missing? Fix that before spelling.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Retells the whole story with no opinion
misconceptions.description: Writes everything that happens in the book, 'First... then... then...', but never says what they thought of it.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Allow one sentence for what the book is about, then start the next with 'I think' or 'I liked'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives an opinion without a reason
misconceptions.description: Writes 'I liked this book. It was good.' with no 'because' and no part of the book named.
misconceptions.repair_hint: After every opinion, add 'because' and name one part of the book that made you feel that way.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives an opinion but does not say what the book is about
misconceptions.description: Writes 'This is the best book ever because it is funny' and a reader still does not know what happens in it.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Start with 'This book is about...' and name the main character and what they want.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves a mistake unfixed
misconceptions.description: Corrects some mistakes but copies others as they were, e.g. fixes 'plaied' but leaves 'frends'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the writing three times: once for spelling, once for full stops and capitals, once for sense.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Changes a word that was already right
misconceptions.description: Changes a correct word into a wrong one while correcting, e.g. changes 'their' to 'there' when 'their' was right.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Before changing a word, say why it is wrong; if there is no reason, leave it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Fixes spelling but not grammar
misconceptions.description: Corrects the spelling slips but leaves 'we was' or 'she go' unchanged.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read each sentence aloud; if it sounds wrong when spoken, check the verb.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes an ending that does not fit the story
misconceptions.description: The new ending forgets what happened or makes a character act unlike themselves, such as a shy boy suddenly shouting at the class.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Before writing, list two things already true in the story and keep both true in your ending.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Retells the original ending
misconceptions.description: Copies or retells the story's own ending, such as the crow dropping pebbles again, when asked for a different one.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Underline the original ending, then decide one thing that will be different in yours.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Stops the story suddenly
misconceptions.description: Ends with 'and then it was all a dream' or 'The end' with no real solution to the problem.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Say how the problem is solved and how the character feels at the very end.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Copies whole sentences as notes
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Peacocks have long tails of shining blue and green feathers.' in a box that needs 'blue and green'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask what the box needs, then cross out every word that is not the answer.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Puts a fact in the wrong box
misconceptions.description: Writes where the bird sleeps in the box for where it lives, or the problem in the ending box.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read each label as a question and check your note answers that question.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Records a small detail instead of the key fact
misconceptions.description: Notes 'warm sea' for what brings the rain, instead of 'strong winds'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask which words the reader would need if they read only your notes.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Puts events out of order
misconceptions.description: Numbers the lamps being placed before the floor is swept, or the result before its cause.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Find the linking word in each sentence and ask what must have happened just before it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Uses a link that gives the wrong meaning
misconceptions.description: Writes 'It rained, because the drains blocked' or 'He was tired, so he kept running' where the link does not fit.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the two ideas aloud with the link and ask: is it time, cause or contrast?

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Uses story narration between the lines
misconceptions.description: Adds sentences such as 'Then Aman went home sadly.' that no actor can say.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Turn the narration into a line or a stage direction: '(walks home slowly)'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Chooses a plan that does not suit the writing
misconceptions.description: Plans instructions for washing hands on a story mountain with a problem and a resolution.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask what the writing is for: a story needs a mountain, a report needs headings, instructions need steps.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes the whole piece instead of a plan
misconceptions.description: Fills the plan with long sentences, such as 'Once upon a time there was a girl called Tanvi who…'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Write only key words for each part; you will turn them into sentences later.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Names a trait with no detail from the story
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Aditya is kind' but gives no action or words from the story that show it.
misconceptions.repair_hint: After each trait, add 'I know this because…' and a detail from the story.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Describes only how the character looks
misconceptions.description: Writes about plaits, height and clothes but nothing about personality, likes or what they say.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Check the profile has all four parts: looks, personality, likes and a quote.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives an opinion with no reason
misconceptions.description: Writes 'I like it here. It is good.' with no because and no detail.
misconceptions.repair_hint: After the opinion, add because and one thing you can see or that happened.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes about the character instead of as the character
misconceptions.description: Writes 'Bunty thinks the flat is small' instead of 'I think this flat is small'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Pretend you are the character: use I, me and my, and words they would use.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Describes the place but gives no opinion
misconceptions.description: Writes 'The flat has two rooms and a balcony' without saying what the character thinks of it.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Add one sentence that says how the character feels about it: love, hate, worry.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Writes in a tone that does not suit the reader
misconceptions.description: Writes to the principal as to a friend: 'Hey! We totally need a bigger playground.'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Think who will read it: start with Dear, use polite words, and end with your name.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Changes side partway through
misconceptions.description: Starts 'We should have a longer lunch break' and ends 'but a short break is better too'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Write your view in one sentence first, and check every reason supports it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves an apostrophe mistake uncorrected
misconceptions.description: Leaves 'Arjuns bag' or 'dont' as written, or writes 'it's' where 'its' is needed.
misconceptions.repair_hint: For each word ending in s, ask: does something belong to it? For short forms, find the missing letter.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves a spelling mistake uncorrected
misconceptions.description: Fixes the grammar but leaves 'becuase', 'freind' or 'untill' as written.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the passage again slowly, one word at a time, pointing at each word.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Leaves a verb or grammar mistake uncorrected
misconceptions.description: Leaves 'they was', 'we goes' or 'buyed' as written.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Find who did the action and say the verb aloud with them: they were, we went.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Changes a word that was already right
misconceptions.description: Changes the correct 'practised' to 'practiced' or 'club's' to 'clubs'.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Only change a word if you can say what rule it breaks.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Fixes one thing but adds a new mistake
misconceptions.description: Rewrites 'Yesterday I go' as 'Yesterday I goed', fixing the tense but adding a wrong verb.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Proofread your new sentence for spelling, tense and punctuation before you finish.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Swaps the meanings of fiction and non-fiction
misconceptions.description: Puts a book of true facts under fiction and a made-up story under non-fiction: 'All About Mangoes' sorted as fiction.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Fiction is made up, like a fib; non-fiction is not made up. Say it before each choice.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Calls a story true because it has real places or things in it
misconceptions.description: Calls a story non-fiction because it is set in Pune or has cricket in it, though a mango sings or a bat hits the moon.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: could this really happen? A real place in a story does not make the story true.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Thinks a book about animals or with pictures must be a story
misconceptions.description: Calls a book of tiger facts fiction because it is about an animal or has pictures: 'The tiger is the largest wild cat' sorted as fiction.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Look for facts you could check, not for animals or pictures; many fact books are full of both.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Shelves a book by one word in its title, not its subject
misconceptions.description: Puts 'Stars of the Kitchen: Easy Indian Recipes' on the space shelf because of the word stars.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Read the whole title and the cover line, then ask what the book teaches you about.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Calls a true account a story because it tells events in order
misconceptions.description: Calls a true diary or a recount of a school trip fiction because it tells what happened, day by day, like a story.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask whether the events really happened to a real person; true events told in order are still non-fiction.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Puts a story on a subject shelf because of what it is about
misconceptions.description: Shelves 'A Cricket Match on Mars' with the sport books, or a story about an elephant with the animal books.
misconceptions.repair_hint: First decide made up or true; only true books go to a subject section.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Builds a fiction label from the wrong part of the book
misconceptions.description: Writes FIC PRI (the author's first name) or FIC NIG (the title) for a story by Priya Kulkarni, instead of FIC KUL.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Find the author's surname, the last name, and take its first three letters.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Names the kind of story from one detail and ignores the rest
misconceptions.description: Calls a story about the Moon's spots a fable, or a detective story an adventure, from one feature only.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Check two or three features before naming the kind: characters, what happens, and how it ends.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Calls any story with animals a fable
misconceptions.description: Calls a myth about a peacock or an adventure with bats a fable, though there is no lesson at the end.
misconceptions.repair_hint: A fable needs animals that act like people and a lesson; look for the lesson before you say fable.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Retells the story instead of naming its features
misconceptions.description: Asked how they know it is a fable, writes 'The peacock was proud and the crow helped him' with no feature named.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Start with 'It is a … because it has …' and name a feature, then give the part of the story that shows it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Describes only one of the two stories when asked to compare
misconceptions.description: Asked how two stories are different, writes only about the fable and says nothing about the adventure.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Use a two-column plan: one fact about each story for every feature, then join them with 'but' or 'while'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up what a non-fiction text is for
misconceptions.description: Says a recipe tells what happened, or that a text about why it rains is a recount.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask what the reader does after reading: follow steps (instructs), learn facts (reports), hear what happened (recounts), or understand why (explains).

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives what the text is about, not what it is for
misconceptions.description: Says two texts about mangoes do the same job because both are about mangoes.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Cover the topic word and ask what the writer wants the reader to do or know.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Matches a feature to the wrong job
misconceptions.description: Says time words like 'yesterday' show instructions, or that chapters show the steps in order.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Point to the feature in a real text and say aloud what it helps the reader do.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Picks a plain fact as the part that keeps the reader interested
misconceptions.description: Chooses 'Bees drink nectar from flowers' instead of the question 'Did you know that a honeybee has five eyes?'
misconceptions.repair_hint: Look for the parts that speak to the reader: questions, fun facts, exclamations and pictures.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up the title and a heading
misconceptions.description: Says 'Sports Day', a heading over one part, is the title of the whole newsletter.
misconceptions.repair_hint: The title names the whole text and comes first; a heading names one part and sits above it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Mixes up stage directions and spoken words
misconceptions.description: Thinks the words in brackets are said aloud, or picks a character's line as the stage direction.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Act it out: say only the words after the name; do what the brackets tell you.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Chooses numbers or bullet points without asking if order matters
misconceptions.description: Numbers a packing list where order does not matter, or gives bullet points for steps that must be done in order.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask: would it go wrong if I did these in a different order? Yes means numbers; no means bullet points.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Gives a text a feature that belongs to another kind of text
misconceptions.description: Says a report is split into verses, or that a stage direction belongs in a report about the monsoon.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Sort feature cards under poem, playscript, report and instructions before answering.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Groups sentences by a shared word, not a shared idea
misconceptions.description: Puts 'We visit the waterfalls' with sentences about the rain because both mention water.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Say in three words what each sentence is about, then group the ideas, not the words.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Chooses a heading that fits only one sentence
misconceptions.description: Chooses 'Making a Rangoli' for a paragraph about cleaning, painting and making a rangoli before Diwali.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Test the heading against every sentence: it must fit them all.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Misses the sentence that does not belong
misconceptions.description: In a paragraph about how a banyan grows, picks a sentence about its roots as the odd one and leaves the sentence about village meetings.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Name the paragraph's one idea first, then check each sentence against it.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Treats a persuading device as plain information
misconceptions.description: Says '9 out of 10 dentists' is there to tell how many tubes are in a box, or underlines the opening times as persuasive words.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask of each part: does it tell me a plain fact, or try to make me want something?

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Says an advert or review is only there to tell a story or give facts
misconceptions.description: Says an advert begins with a question 'to tell a story', or that a review is trying to sell places.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask who wrote it and what they want you to do: buy, visit, or decide.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Copies a persuasive word without saying how it works
misconceptions.description: Writes 'thrilling' as the answer but does not say it makes the ride sound exciting so you want to go.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Use the frame: 'The writer uses … to make the reader feel or think …'.

misconceptions.subject: ENG
misconceptions.name: Believes an advert's claims as facts
misconceptions.description: Says the advert is right that the camp is never crowded, though the review says it was very crowded.
misconceptions.repair_hint: Ask who gains if you believe it, and check the claim against another text.
